summary_paragraph: A 59-year-old woman with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis and HIV presented with a partially dislodged right femoral tunneled dialysis catheter, preventing scheduled dialysis. She also reported nontraumatic pain in her left first and second toes. The catheter was successfully exchanged over a wire in the interventional radiology suite without complications. Hemodialysis was completed the following day using the new catheter. Foot X-ray showed no fracture, and the toe pain was managed symptomatically. The patient initially refused her home HIV medications but was counseled on adherence and agreed to resume treatment. She was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to monitor the catheter site and maintain medication compliance.
